Sampled HR@10 can reverse full-catalog model rankings; preserve the pinned evaluator and restrict claims to its fixed users/candidates ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Recommended design: preregister the four ablations, preprocessing/training/evaluation seeds 0/42/42, hyperparameter ranges, checkpoint schedule, stopping rules and macro-average selection rule. Count every inspected checkpoint as a selection opportunity, including category-specific choices; equalize search opportunities across ablations and log unsuccessful trials. Repeatedly maximizing noisy validation scores creates selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Use sparse, fixed checkpoint evaluations and a predetermined tie-break favoring simpler or earlier models.

Retain each user’s binary hit for every model. For paired uncertainty, resample the same user indices across models within each category, preserving 200 users/category, then recompute the equally weighted four-category mean difference; report paired 95% bootstrap intervals and category-level differences. Bootstrap/randomization methods have support in recommendation evaluation ([Ihemelandu–Ekstrand](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale)). One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on fixed training seeds and candidate sets; they neither measure training/negative-sampling variability nor correct winner-selection optimism. For prespecified comparisons, use Holm correction; treat intervals for adaptively selected winners as descriptive.

Compute recommendation: profile actual GPU-seconds per dataset/model first. The budget is 12 aggregate GPU-hours; four slots reduce elapsed time, not expenditure. Reserve a contingency/final-training allowance, give all four ablations initial coverage on every dataset, then promote complete four-dataset configurations at predetermined macro-score rungs. Successive halving supports this allocation strategy ([Hyperband](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06560)). Budget by measured time rather than equal epochs; count diagnostics and failures, protect slower datasets from premature elimination, and retain seed 42. Never consult test labels.
